source.description:
POST-MERGE FIELD FINDING — squash-merged worktrees are held forever by the predicate.

Observed 2026-08-06 while tearing down this programme's lanes. The darth-feedor lane worktree carried commit caad1c4 "fix(cd): build mercury-base when absent...". `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` reported 1, so the no-unpushed-commits condition FAILED and the worktree was held. But that commit IS in main, as 226c9ab, merged via squash in PR #191 — identical subject, different sha.

Neither of the predicate's two accepted forms recognises this:
  - "zero unpushed commits vs upstream" — false, the squash rewrote the sha
  - "branch is an ancestor of origin/HEAD" — false, for the same reason

So any repo using squash-merge produces worktrees the reaper can never reclaim. It is a FALSE HOLD, not a false reap, so it is safe — it fails closed, which is the right direction. But on a squash-merge repo the reaper's effective yield drops toward zero, and the accumulation this bead exists to fix continues silently while the tool reports it is working. That is the failure mode worth caring about: a guard that is safe and useless looks identical to a guard that is safe and effective.

Suggested third accepted form, in addition to the two existing ones:
  - every commit in `origin/main..HEAD` has a subject-and-patch-id match already in origin/main
`git cherry origin/main HEAD` answers this directly and is the idiomatic test — it marks commits with '-' when an equivalent change is already upstream regardless of sha. A branch whose every commit is marked '-' is fully merged, squash or not.

Recommend verifying against a repo that squash-merges before implementing, and adding a regression test with a squash-merged branch fixture. This programme's own repos differ: mercury/infra and dev/core merge with merge commits, darth-feedor squashes — so both paths are exercised in the field today.

Recorded from orchestrator teardown, not from a lane. Both held worktrees were inspected by hand and removed after confirming the work was upstream; no data was lost. The other held worktree (dev/core) was dirty only in .xtrm/skills/state.json and .specialists/user, both tooling scaffolding — the reaper's own exclusion list already covers those, so it was correct there and my ad-hoc teardown filter was the thing that was too narrow.
source.title: [bug] xt worktree reap holds squash-merged worktrees forever — predicate has no patch-equivalence test
